findings.title: No-JS fallback renders the only submit button disabled; step-6 'full submit succeeds' is evidenced only by curl, so a real JS-disabled browser cannot submit — contradicts 'Defects found: none — clean pass'
findings.evidence: review_consent.gleam: attribute("disabled", ""), on the submit-application button (unconditional, present since d1a0804/PR #97); committed 17-nojs-long-form.html: <button class="btn-submit" data-testid="submit-application" disabled type="submit">; form.js:26 submit.disabled = ... (JS is the only enabler); zero <noscript> in server/src + priv/static
findings.detail: The SSR no-JS page renders submit disabled and only JS re-enables it (consent gate). The pass's curl POST bypasses the button, so journey step 6's 'full submit succeeds' is not demonstrated for a real no-JS browser, and the pass declared 'Defects found: none' instead of halting/escalating per the briefing. Pre-existing app behavior, but catching exactly this was the pass's job.
findings.recommended_fix: Product decision needed: either render submit enabled when JS is absent (noscript-aware SSR) so the no-JS fallback truly submits, or drop/amend the no-JS-submit claim; evidence must use a real JS-disabled browser (or document the curl limitation). Escalate the disabled-submit dead-end per the briefing's defect rule.

findings.title: README/notes claim application_draft_resumed fires at load on the resume page, but the committed capture records no such event
findings.evidence: 21-analytics-notes.md: 'the resume page fires application_draft_resumed at load (payload {vacancy_short_code} only)'; 20-analytics-resume-page.json resumePageEvents = 15 x $autocapture + 1 x application_draft_saved (16 events, zero draft_resumed)
findings.detail: apply_analytics.js fires application_draft_resumed on marker form-resume; the committed resume-page capture does not contain it (possibly fired before the in-page wrapper was installed — either way the committed evidence does not show it).
findings.recommended_fix: Re-capture with the wrapper installed before navigation, or amend the README/notes to state the event is code-pinned but not present in the committed stream.

findings.title: round-trip.yaml description claims resumed_at coverage but no flow step asserts it
findings.evidence: description: 'resumed_at stamping on the first post-resume save'; Flow steps 1-7 assert draft row/continue_token, sent status, banner, value restore, stepper landing, confirmation — no resumed_at assertion
findings.detail: The canonical F3 scenario advertises resumed_at coverage it never exercises; a resumed_at regression would pass this scenario.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a DB assertion step after the first post-resume save (same token-seam psql pattern as step 3) or trim the description.

findings.title: {SCENARIO} 64-char local-part truncation silently eats {RUN_ID} digits — rapid re-runs of long-slug scenarios collide as duplicate applications
findings.evidence: 'the whole local part truncated to 64 chars'; verified math: test+validation-missing-guarantor-when-first-time-renter-1785759182 = 67 chars, test+edge-cases-stacked-conditionals-student-firsttime-... = 65 — truncation to 64 eats 1-3 RUN_ID digits
findings.detail: With RUN_ID (epoch seconds) truncated, two runs within the same ~1000s window produce the same email for the 3 longest-slug scenarios; the second run hits duplicate-notice instead of the expected outcome. SKILL.md wording does not say to preserve RUN_ID.
findings.recommended_fix: Truncate the slug portion, not the RUN_ID (e.g. slug capped at 64-5-1-10=48 chars, RUN_ID always preserved), and say so in SKILL.md.

findings.title: generate-fixtures.sh fails on any checkout lacking fixtures/ (set -eu + cd into gitignored dir) — the migration re-breaks existing working copies at the new .pi path
findings.evidence: script: 'set -eu' + 'cd "$(dirname "$0")/fixtures"' with no mkdir -p; fresh worktree at reviewed sha: helpers/ contains only generate-fixtures.sh (fixtures/ gitignored, never committed)
findings.detail: Pre-existing for fresh clones, but the migration makes it hit every existing working copy: untracked fixtures/ stays behind at the old .claude path while the new .pi path has none, so the documented preflight (bash generate-fixtures.sh) exits non-zero until someone manually mkdirs.
findings.recommended_fix: Add 'mkdir -p "$(dirname "$0")/fixtures"' before the cd (or commit a .gitkeep).

findings.title: README claims no-JS render has 'no hidden attrs' — committed 17-nojs-long-form.html contains 8 hidden attributes, and conditional content is unreachable without JS
findings.evidence: README: 'GET renders all 8 data-section-id with no hidden attrs'; committed HTML: 3 x income-source-row ... hidden + data-condition="co_applicant_sharing" ... hidden wrappers (8 exact hidden attributes)
findings.detail: The 8 section fieldsets are indeed unhidden, but the unqualified claim is contradicted by the artifact; without JS a no-JS user can never reveal co-applicant upload slots or extra income rows (pre-existing progressive-disclosure pattern).
findings.recommended_fix: Amend the README claim to 'all 8 sections render unhidden; conditional/optional blocks remain hidden without JS (by design)'.

findings.title: Acceptance requires suites green 'BEFORE and AFTER your pass' — README documents only the BEFORE baseline
findings.evidence: Briefing Acceptance: 'all make test / make test-integration suites green on develop BEFORE and AFTER your pass'; README: 'Unit + integration baselines BEFORE the pass: make test green ... 377 integration tests green' — no AFTER re-run recorded
findings.detail: Zero application-code changes make the risk nil, but the acceptance criterion explicitly names both endpoints and only one is documented.
findings.recommended_fix: Run make test / test-integration post-pass and record the result (one line in the README).

findings.title: Save-resume (step 5) DB claims cite uncommitted 'verify-run DB checks' — no draft/resume DB dump in the evidence directory

findings.title: Pre-existing duplicate data-section="5" in SSR markup (guarantor + tell_us_more) — inert, no JS consumer
findings.evidence: guarantor.gleam: attribute("data-section", "5"); tell_us_more.gleam: attribute("data-section", "5"); numbering runs 1,2,3,4,5,5,6,7; grep shows only data-section-id is consumed (apply_analytics.js, form_stepper.js)
